name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.application.UseApplicationBlockForConventionProperties
displayName: Move the `application` convention properties into the `application { }` block
description: `ApplicationPluginConvention` is deprecated since Gradle 8.2 and removed in Gradle 9, so assigning `applicationName`, `applicationDefaultJvmArgs` or `executableDir` on the project warns on Gradle 8.14 in Groovy, fails on Gradle 9 in Groovy with `Could not set unknown property`, and does not compile in Kotlin on Gradle 8.14 or 9. name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.MigrateHttpRepositories
displayName: Use HTTPS or allow the insecure protocol for `http://` repositories
description: Gradle 7.0 rejects repositories with an `http://` URL unless they opt in to the insecure protocol. A repository on a well-known public host that also serves HTTPS, such as Maven Central, the Gradle Plugin Portal or the Aliyun mirror, switches to `https://`. Any other `http://` repository, such as an internal repository manager or `localhost`, keeps its URL and gets `allowInsecureProtocol = true`, or `isAllowInsecureProtocol = true` in the Kotlin DSL, so the build keeps resolving from it.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.OneDependencyDeclarationPerStatement
displayName: Use one dependency declaration per statement
description: The Gradle Groovy DSL accepts multiple coordinates in a single configuration call (e.g. `implementation 'a:b:1.0', 'c:d:2.0'`), but the Kotlin DSL does not. Gradle's best practices recommend declaring a single dependency per statement; see the [Gradle dependency best practices](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_dependencies.html). This recipe splits multi-coordinate Groovy DSL configuration calls into one call per coordinate. Run this as a cleanup pass before other dependency-aware recipes (e.g. `UpgradeDependencyVersion`, `ChangeDependency`, `RemoveDependency`): those recipes use the `GradleDependency` trait, which only inspects the first argument of a configuration call. Coordinates in later positions are invisible to them until this recipe reshapes the source into one declaration per statement.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.RemoveConfigurationVisible
displayName: Remove the deprecated `Configuration.visible` property
description: `Configuration.visible` has had no effect since Gradle 9.0, and is deprecated for removal in Gradle 11. Gradle 9.8.2 warns on `setVisible` where Gradle 8.14.4 does not. name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.RemoveExplicitKotlinStdlibDependency
displayName: Remove explicit Kotlin standard library dependency
description: The Kotlin Gradle plugin adds the version of `kotlin-stdlib` that matches itself, so declaring the dependency explicitly is redundant. Removes `org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib` and its `-jdk7`, `-jdk8` and `-common` variants, written either as coordinates or with the Kotlin DSL `kotlin("stdlib")` helper, from a project that applies a Kotlin plugin. Only `implementation` declarations are removed, because that is the one configuration the Kotlin plugin contributes the standard library to: a declaration on `api` is consumer-visible through the published compile scope, and one on a configuration of the project's own has nothing putting it back. A declaration is kept when it pins a version newer than the plugin's, since removing it would quietly downgrade the standard library; when the plugin predates 1.4, the first version that adds the standard library itself; and when `kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency=false` turns that default off, leaving the declaration as the only thing providing it. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_dependencies.html#dont_depend_on_kotlin_stdlib).

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.RemoveInheritedDependencies
displayName: Remove dependencies already inherited from an extended configuration
description: Remove a dependency declaration whose configuration already receives the same dependency from a configuration it extends. `testImplementation` extends `implementation`, and in `java-library` `implementation` extends `api`, so declaring one coordinate on both reaches nothing the wider declaration did not already reach â€” the second line only has to be kept in step with the first. The declaration on the extending configuration is the one removed, leaving the widest. Declarations whose versions differ are left alone, since removing one of those changes which version resolves, and configurations unrelated by `extendsFrom`, such as `compileOnly` beside `implementation`, express two intentions rather than a duplicate. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_dependencies.html#avoid_duplicate_dependencies).

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.RewriteSpreadAllInConfigurationsBlock
displayName: Replace spread-`all*` calls in `configurations` blocks with `configurations.all { }`
description: Gradle 9 throws `Cannot mutate the dependencies of configuration ':all' after the configuration was resolved.` when a `configurations { }` closure uses Groovy's spread-dot form `all*.<method>(args)`. Rewrite each such call to the closure form `configurations.all { <method>(args) }`, which preserves eager-`all` semantics but is accepted by Gradle 9. In mixed blocks, contiguous spread calls are grouped in `all { }` closures, leaving named configurations and other statements in place.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.UseAssembleDependsOnInsteadOfArchives
displayName: Make `assemble` depend on a task instead of adding it to the `archives` configuration
description: Gradle 9.1 deprecates adding artifacts to the `archives` configuration, which will fail in Gradle 10. What the declaration does is have `assemble` build the artifact, so this recipe replaces `artifacts { archives x }` with `tasks.named("assemble") { dependsOn(x) }`, as the upgrade guide says. Files, maps and a declaration with a configuration closure are left alone, and so is every script that mentions `uploadArchives` or otherwise reads the `archives` configuration, such as `sign configurations.archives`, since those depend on its artifacts. See the [Gradle upgrade guide](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/upgrading_version_9.html#archives-configuration) for more information.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.UseAssignmentForRepositoryUrl
displayName: Use `=` assignment syntax for a repository's `url`
description: Setting a property with the Gradle-generated `propName value` syntax is deprecated since Gradle 8.14 and scheduled for removal in Gradle 10. displayName: Use `extendsFrom` instead of a `Configuration` as a dependency
description: Gradle 8.0 no longer allows a `Configuration` in the `dependencies { }` block, failing with `Adding a Configuration as a dependency is no longer allowed as of Gradle 8.0`. A declaration with a configuration closure, a configuration of another project, and a name the script also uses for a variable are left alone. name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.artifacts.UseGetOnConfigurationAccessors
displayName: Call `get()` on Kotlin DSL configuration accessors
description: Gradle 8.0 removed the Kotlin DSL extensions that let a script reach the members of a `Configuration` directly from a `NamedDomainObjectProvider<Configuration>`, so `configurations.compileClasspath.files` fails to compile with `Unresolved reference: files`. displayName: Use `mavenCentral()` instead of `jcenter()`
description: `RepositoryHandler.jcenter()` was deprecated in Gradle 7.0 and removed in Gradle 9.0. displayName: Use `project(...)` dependency notation instead of the current project's module coordinates
description: Gradle 9.3 deprecates depending on the current project by its own `group:name:version` module coordinates. name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.plugins.MigratePluginPublishPlugin
displayName: Migrate the Plugin Publish plugin to 1.x
description: `com.gradle.plugin-publish` before 1.0 calls `Jar.getArchivePath()` and `DefaultDecoratedConvention`, removed in Gradle 8 and 9, so applying it fails with "Failed to notify project evaluation listener" once the wrapper is upgraded. Version 1.0 removed the `pluginBundle { }` block in turn, so bumping the version alone fails with "Could not find method pluginBundle()". This recipe does both at once: it moves `website` and `vcsUrl` onto `gradlePlugin`, and `description`, `displayName` and `tags` onto each plugin `gradlePlugin { plugins { } }` declares, then removes `pluginBundle` and upgrades the plugin to 1.3.1. `tags = [..]` on the declaration needs Gradle 8.2 or later, which `MigrateToGradle8` upgrades to. A script with no `gradlePlugin { plugins { } }` of its own, which declares its plugins only in `pluginBundle { plugins { } }`, has that block written for it, taking each `implementationClass` from the checked-in `META-INF/gradle-plugins/<id>.properties` descriptor, which is then deleted: Gradle generates it from the declaration, and a checked-in copy of what it generates makes `processResources` fail on a duplicate entry from Gradle 7 on. A redundant descriptor is deleted for a plugin the script already declares, too. A script this recipe cannot migrate in full keeps its old plugin version, rather than being left bumped and broken: that is a `pluginBundle` holding `mavenCoordinates`, a `version` other than the project's, or anything else unrecognized, a declaration in `pluginBundle { plugins { } }` with no counterpart in `gradlePlugin { plugins { } }`, and a plugin declared in neither block or with no descriptor to take its implementation class from. Kotlin scripts are left alone. See the [plugin-publish 1.0 release notes](https://plugins.gradle.org/docs/publish-plugin) for more information.

description: Move a build script's top-level `repositories` block into `dependencyResolutionManagement` in the settings file, so the build has one place that says where dependencies come from and a project cannot quietly resolve from somewhere the rest of the build does not. name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseDefaultPathSensitivity
displayName: Declare path sensitivity on task file inputs
description: Annotate an `@InputFile` with `@PathSensitive(PathSensitivity.NONE)` and an `@InputDirectory` with `@PathSensitive(PathSensitivity.RELATIVE)`, and replace `PathSensitivity.ABSOLUTE` with those values. Absolute paths are the default when no sensitivity is declared, which puts the checkout location into the task's cache key: the same inputs then miss the build cache on another machine, or in another directory on the same one. `@InputFiles` is left alone because the right sensitivity for a collection depends on whether the task cares about the names within it, which the annotation does not say. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_tasks.html#default_path_sensitivities).

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseFilePermissions
displayName: Use `filePermissions` and `dirPermissions` instead of `fileMode` and `dirMode`
description: `CopyProcessingSpec.fileMode` and `dirMode` are deprecated since Gradle 8.8 and removed in Gradle 9, where setting them fails. `filePermissions { unix(..) }` and `dirPermissions { unix(..) }` exist since Gradle 8.3. Integer literals inside `Copy`, `Sync`, archive task and copy spec blocks are moved as they are written, so Groovy's octal `0644` stays `0644` and Kotlin's decimal `420` stays `420`, both the same permission bits. Computed values such as `"755".toInt(8)`, reads, `details.mode`, unknown task types and Nebula's packaging tasks are left alone. See the [Gradle upgrade guide](https://docs.gradle.org/9.0.0/userguide/upgrading_major_version_9.html#removal_of_unix_mode_based_file_permissions) for more information.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseMainClassProperty
displayName: Use `mainClass` instead of `main` for `JavaExec` tasks
description: The `main` property on `JavaExec` tasks was deprecated in Gradle 7.1. Kotlin scripts stop compiling on it in Gradle 8.0 and Groovy scripts fail on it in Gradle 9.0. Use the `mainClass` property instead. See the [Gradle upgrade guide](https://docs.gradle.org/8.14/userguide/upgrading_version_7.html#v7_java_exec_api_cleanup) for more information.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseMatchingInsteadOfFindAll
displayName: Use `matching(Closure)` instead of `findAll(Closure)` on Gradle container collections
description: Gradle 9.4 deprecates the Groovy `DomainObjectCollection.findAll(Closure)` overload on containers such as `tasks`, `configurations`, and `sourceSets`. It is replaced by the lazy `DomainObjectCollection.matching(Closure)`, which returns a live collection that only filters elements as they are needed by the build. This recipe only swaps the method name, leaving the closure argument unchanged, rewriting `findAll { ... }` to `matching { ... }` when the receiver is a known Gradle container collection.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseNamedInsteadOfStringInvoke
displayName: Use `named("x")` instead of `"x"()` in the Kotlin DSL
description: Looking up a domain object with `"x"()` in the Kotlin DSL is deprecated and does not compile on Gradle 9. `named("x")` returns the same provider. `"x"(Type::class)` and `"x" { }` are still supported, so only the form with no arguments and no lambda changes. A call inside `withGroovyBuilder { }` is a Groovy-builder invocation on the receiver rather than a container lookup, so it is left alone. Groovy is not affected. See the [Gradle upgrade guide](https://docs.gradle.org/8.14/userguide/upgrading_version_8.html#string_invoke) for more information.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseTaskPropertiesForPluginConventions
displayName: Configure the `war`, `ear` and project report tasks instead of their plugin conventions
description: `WarPluginConvention`, `EarPluginConvention` and `ProjectReportsPluginConvention` are deprecated since Gradle 8.2 and removed in Gradle 9, so assigning `webAppDirName`, `appDirName`, `libDirName` or `projectReportDirName` on the project warns on Gradle 8.14 in Groovy, fails on Gradle 9 in Groovy, and does not compile in Kotlin on Gradle 8.14 or 9. Each assignment becomes configuration of the task, as the upgrade guide says. A script that declares its own `War` or `Ear` task gets `tasks.withType(..).configureEach { }`, because the convention reached those tasks too and `war { }` would not. The replacement for `projectReportDirName` moves only the HTML dependency report: on Gradle 8.14 and 9.8 the text reports of `projectReport` stay in `build/reports/project`. Only a literal `projectReportDirName` is changed. Reads, and a script's own `def`, `val` or `ext` of the same name, are left alone. See the [Gradle upgrade guide](https://docs.gradle.org/8.14/userguide/upgrading_version_8.html#war_convention_deprecation) for more information.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.tasks.UseWritePropertiesDestinationFile
displayName: Use `destinationFile` instead of `outputFile` on `WriteProperties` tasks
description: `WriteProperties.outputFile` is deprecated and removed in Gradle 9, where setting it fails. `destinationFile` replaces it. Only assignments directly in a block that names the `WriteProperties` type change. A string value is wrapped in `file(..)`, because Gradle 8.14 does not accept a string for `destinationFile`. Reads are left alone, since `destinationFile` is a `Provider` rather than a `File`. See the [Gradle upgrade guide](https://docs.gradle.org/9.0.0/userguide/upgrading_major_version_9.html) for more information.

name: org.openrewrite.gradle.migrate.wrapper.AddGradleWrapperChecksum
displayName: Add the Gradle distribution SHA-256 checksum
description: Pin the SHA-256 checksum of the Gradle distribution the wrapper already downloads, by adding `distributionSha256Sum` to `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` when it is absent. Without it the wrapper runs whatever the distribution URL happens to serve. The sum is fetched from the distribution URL with `.sha256` appended, which is how Gradle publishes it, so `distributionUrl` is left exactly as it is and the Gradle version does not change. `org.openrewrite.gradle.UpdateGradleWrapper` also pins the sum, but as part of moving the wrapper to the version it resolves; use this recipe to pin the version already in the file. See the [Gradle best practice](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/best_practices_security.html#validate_gradle_checksum).
